clue.text: Predict how to succeed cutting wood

indicators.note: to succeed means to come after, so this piece follows the trimmed wood
cutting here means trimming the last letter off the word for wood

parts.note: a forest is a wood
taken as written

explanation.surface: Advice on how to get ahead in the timber trade, foretold.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cutting' is not a wood product here: it shortens the wood word by its last letter, and 'to succeed' means to follow, not to prosper.
explanation.definitionFit: To foreshow is an old verb for foretelling or prophesying what will come.

clue.text: The same old bird heard to say "one left"

parts.note: e.g. (for example) is the abbreviation used for 'say'
a means one, the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A familiar old bird is heard announcing that one has departed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bird heard' adds a hint that the answer sounds rather like 'eagle'; the letters come from EG, A and L. The word is archaic, hence 'old'.
explanation.definitionFit: Egal is an obsolete English word, from French, meaning equal or alike.

clue.text: Apt line-up of solver

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the line word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: a row is a line
thy is the old form of 'your', belonging to you the solver

explanation.surface: A suitable set of puzzlers arranged in a row.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns ROW into WOR; THY, the archaic 'your', addresses the solver.
explanation.definitionFit: Worthy means deserving or fitting, close to apt in the sense of suitable.

clue.text: A number in lottery at new place on Thames

indicators.note: in signals that the number goes inside the lottery game

parts.note: bingo is a game of chance with numbered draws, a kind of lottery
D is the Roman numeral for 500, a number

explanation.surface: A lucky number comes up in a draw at a fresh spot by the river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts D inside BINGO for BINGDO.
explanation.definitionFit: Abingdon is a market town on the River Thames in Oxfordshire, England.

clue.text: Read other than arts subjects with monitor

parts.note: to con is to study or read over closely
the sciences are the subjects set against the arts

explanation.surface: A student studies science rather than the humanities, under supervision.
explanation.definitionFit: Conscience is the inner sense of right and wrong that monitors one's own conduct.

clue.text: Way to get round horses — pearls?

parts.note: St is the abbreviation for street, a way
to ring is to encircle or get round something

explanation.surface: A route that loops around the stables, with a hint of jewellery.
explanation.definitionFit: A string is a set of racehorses from one stable, and also a strand of threaded pearls.

clue.text: Silver complement perhaps to 23, singularly warmer

definitions.meaning: the pirate Silver in Stevenson's novel has a first name and nickname that set long against the short of the politician at 23
thermal leggings worn under trousers, usually spoken of as a plural pair, here as one garment

explanation.definitionFit: Long johns are warm underwear; as a name it gives the pirate Long John Silver, set against Short.

clue.text: Nul points is proverbially encouraging

parts.note: nul is French for none, as in Eurovision's nul points
W and S are points of the compass, west and south

explanation.surface: Scoring nothing at Eurovision is, so the saying goes, a good sign.
explanation.walkthrough: The proverb is 'no news is good news'.
explanation.definitionFit: The saying 'no news is good news' makes the phrase a proverbial source of reassurance.

clue.text: Bell of Breton origin

indicators.note: origin hints that the word Breton is the source from which the name was formed, so rearrange it

explanation.surface: A bell made in Brittany.
explanation.walkthrough: The Brontë sisters published as Currer, Ellis and Acton Bell; 'origin' rearranges BRETON.
explanation.definitionFit: Bell was the shared pen surname the Brontë sisters used for their first books.

clue.text: Burns's spirit has reprised 18's oeuvre

indicators.note: reprised suggests playing back, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: the composer at 18 down wrote hundreds of songs, each a Lied in German

explanation.surface: A poet's ghost revisits a composer's works.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reprised' turns LIED into DEIL. Robert Burns, Scotland's national poet, wrote in Scots.
explanation.definitionFit: Deil is the Scots word for the devil, an evil spirit, used by Burns.

clue.text: Several workers' joint occupation

parts.note: ten stands for an unspecified several
worker ants are the classic crossword workers
the hip is a joint of the body

explanation.surface: A team of labourers sharing a cannabis cigarette, or their shared property.
explanation.definitionFit: Tenantship is the occupation or holding of property as a tenant.

clue.text: What happened nearly 130 years ago to Greek character at the end of every game — a bloomer from hell?

parts.note: theta is the eighth letter of the Greek alphabet

indicators.note: at the end of means take the last letter of every

parts.note: bridge is a card game
Dis is the classical underworld, hell
an aster is a flower, something that blooms

explanation.surface: A strange tale of a Greek letter, a game, and a flower sprung from the underworld.
explanation.walkthrough: The Tay rail bridge at Dundee collapsed under a train in December 1879, a disaster famously marked in verse by William McGonagall, often called the worst poet in English.
explanation.definitionFit: The collapse of the Tay rail bridge in 1879 was a famous historical event.

clue.text: Michael after Lew and Leslie?

parts.note: the broadcaster Michael Grade followed his uncle Lew and father Leslie in the Grade show-business family, making him the next one in line

explanation.walkthrough: In US schools the phrase names a year of elementary school, but here it counts members of a family.
explanation.definitionFit: Michael was the third prominent Grade, while the phrase also names a US school year.

clue.text: See 24
Funny fellow with dam to dam again

parts.note: a weir is a dam across a river
do is short for ditto, meaning the same word again

explanation.surface: An odd chap builds one dam and then another.
explanation.walkthrough: 'do.' (ditto) means the same again, so the second 'dam' is a repeat sign.
explanation.definitionFit: A weirdo is an odd or eccentric person, funny in the sense of peculiar.

clue.text: See 12
Darling dog comes in when there's fruit on the ground

indicators.note: comes in signals that the dog goes inside the word for when

parts.note: as can mean when, as in 'as I left'
Nana is the dog of the Darling family in Peter Pan

explanation.surface: A beloved dog arrives when windfalls lie in the orchard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Darling' is not a term of endearment: it is the family name in Peter Pan.
explanation.definitionFit: Ananas is the pineapple, whose fruit grows close to the ground on a low plant.

clue.text: Insert fish — mine was Trout

parts.note: split as In sert, the clue tells you to put a fish, the chub, in the letters sert

explanation.surface: A fishy instruction from a composer whose famous piece was about trout.
explanation.walkthrough: The Trout Quintet is one of Schubert's best-known works.
explanation.definitionFit: Schubert composed the Trout Quintet, so his work was the Trout.

clue.text: Disburse to boy or girl with solvers' entry

indicators.note: entry signals the solvers going inside the name

parts.note: Pat can be short for Patrick or Patricia
the solvers are addressed as you

explanation.surface: Paying out to a child, with the solvers' contribution.
explanation.definitionFit: To pay out is to disburse money, spending it from a fund.

clue.text: Old country hero aids reform

indicators.note: to reform is to shape anew, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A champion helps reform an old nation.
explanation.definitionFit: Rhodesia was the former name of the African country now Zimbabwe.

clue.text: Boy or girl monster reported on line

indicators.note: reported tells you the word is as it is spoken, not spelt

parts.note: the Gila monster is a venomous American lizard, said 'heela'
Ry is the abbreviation for railway, a line

explanation.surface: A child's name and a monster in the news online.
explanation.walkthrough: Gila is pronounced with an H sound; 'on' places RY after it in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Hilary is a given name used for both men and women.

clue.text: Second right for German playwright

parts.note: B denotes second, as in B-class
Recht is German for right

explanation.surface: A second opinion on a German dramatist's rights.
explanation.walkthrough: The German word suits a German playwright.
explanation.definitionFit: Bertolt Brecht was a twentieth-century German dramatist.

clue.text: Take first innings and field afterwards in Yorkshire

indicators.note: afterwards places the field word after the batting

parts.note: in cricket the side batting first takes the first innings
a ley (or lea) is a field of grass

explanation.surface: A cricket captain bats first and then fields, in Yorkshire.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket each side alternately bats and fields.
explanation.definitionFit: Batley is a town in West Yorkshire, England, so it lies in Yorkshire.

clue.text: With wine about, silence golden for politician

indicators.note: about signals the wine going round the other pieces

parts.note: claret is red Bordeaux wine
sh is a call for silence
or is gold in heraldry

explanation.surface: Over drinks, a politician learns that silence is golden.
explanation.walkthrough: Clare Short was a Labour cabinet minister.
explanation.definitionFit: Clare Short was a British Labour MP and cabinet minister, a politician.

clue.text: How 40s celebrate Burns week ending giddy with excitement

indicators.note: excitement suggests agitation, so these letters are shaken up

parts.note: W/E is the abbreviation for week ending

explanation.surface: Couples at forty celebrate Burns Night at the end of a week, giddy and excited.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with excitement' rearranges BURNS, WE and GIDDY.
explanation.definitionFit: A ruby wedding is a fortieth anniversary, so couples married forty years celebrate one.

clue.text: Former part of county — C on Y, say

definitions.meaning: the old Scottish county of the Highlands joined this district with Cromarty until 1975
C sounds like sea, naming an Antarctic sea, and on Y sounds like on Wye, naming a Herefordshire market town on the River Wye

explanation.walkthrough: The printed grid gives ROSE, but the clue only works for ROSS, as blog commenters noted.
explanation.definitionFit: The name belongs to a former Scottish district, an Antarctic sea and a town on the Wye.

clue.text: See 12
Centre section on a certain island

indicators.note: section means a part of the word centre is taken

parts.note: sure means certain

explanation.surface: Something found on a certain island, at its very heart.
explanation.walkthrough: Treasure Island is Stevenson's novel, home of Long John Silver from 7.
explanation.definitionFit: Treasure names Stevenson's island, the first word of Treasure Island.
